old_row.rationale: Kings says no hammer, axe or iron implement was heard during the house construction; Deuteronomy forbids laying iron on altar stones. Temple hearing and altar tool-use restrictions remain distinct, and sharply cut unworked is not rewritten.

new_row.relationship: Carved cherubim and interior palms in the house descriptions

unresolved_candidates.reason: Kings describes the widow's son with he-from-Naphtali wording, a Tyrian father and bronze-working language. Chronicles names Chiram, my father, gives his mother from Dan's daughters and a Tyrian father, and lists broad crafts. The complete passages and context were read. The different tribal clauses, maternal attribution and sentence/pronoun scope are not independently harmonized. The retained parallel credits only the actual Tyrian-parentage and craft-service descriptions, not a solved Naphtali-Dan or other personal-name identity.
unresolved_candidates.retained_pair_scope: Tyrian-parentage and craft-service comparison only; tribal and parentage harmonization excluded

candidate_exclusions.proposed_claim: Force familiar personal/place identities, harmonize construction measurements or duration, translate remaining technical labels, equate bells with pomegranates, reassign ambiguous pronouns, add maternal tribal attribution, or infer absent materials and tool commands.
candidate_exclusions.reason: Retained explanations use bounded actual clauses, explicit comparisons and meaningful source-list dependencies. Read but unretained speculative equations and technical checks receive no completion credit.
